flashcards.q: How is capturing used in Marketing?
flashcards.a: Explain the role of marketing in creating and capturing demand and how it works with sales and product.

flashcards.q: How should sits not be handled in Marketing?
flashcards.a: Most partnerships fail not through conflict but through neglect: neither side assigns an owner, and the agreement sits unused.

flashcards.q: What does Marketing teach about hypothetical?
flashcards.a: All companies, people and figures in the examples and case study are hypothetical and were built for teaching.

flashcards.q: What should be avoided with reminder in Marketing?
flashcards.a: The value of the framework is not the list itself but the reminder that a promotion problem is sometimes really a product, price or availability problem.

flashcards.q: When is reached applied in Marketing?
flashcards.a: Ten to twenty well-run interviews with people in one segment often surface most of the major themes; when new interviews stop producing new themes, you have likely reached saturation for that question.

flashcards.q: When should reminder not be used in Marketing?
flashcards.a: It uses the customer's language, leads with the outcome, states specifics instead of adjectives ("cut no-shows by sending reminders 24 hours and 2 hours before class" rather than "powerful reminder features"), and asks for one action at a time.

flashcards.q: Where does qualitative come up in Marketing?
flashcards.a: Design a market research plan that combines qualitative and quantitative evidence.

flashcards.q: Where does spending not apply in Marketing?
flashcards.a: Marketing mix modeling uses statistical analysis of spending and sales over time to estimate each channel's contribution, and works without tracking individuals, which grows more valuable as privacy rules and browser changes limit user-level tracking.

flashcards.q: Is attribution ever unnecessary in Marketing?
flashcards.a: No attribution model reveals true causation; each embeds an assumption.

flashcards.q: Which approach to copy fits Marketing?
flashcards.a: Listen for the customer's own words, which later become marketing copy.

flashcards.q: Who is involved with deciding in Marketing?
flashcards.a: Marketing is the work of deciding which customers a business will serve, understanding what those customers need, shaping an offer and a message that fits them, and bringing that offer to their attention in ways that lead to profitable, lasting relationships.

flashcards.q: Who should not be handling ends in Marketing?
flashcards.a: A team that only broadcasts and never listens ends up promoting products nobody wants.

flashcards.q: Why does incrementality matter in Marketing?
flashcards.a: Compare attribution models and explain why incrementality matters.

flashcards.q: How is contribution margin used in Marketing?
flashcards.a: Calculate contribution margin and break-even volume and explain how discounts change them.

flashcards.q: What does Marketing teach about qualified?
flashcards.a: Legal topics are described in general terms; confirm the rules for your market with qualified counsel.

flashcards.q: What should be avoided with ready in Marketing?
flashcards.a: The handoff needs a written agreement: what counts as a qualified lead, how quickly sales will follow up, and how leads that are not ready will be returned to nurturing.

flashcards.q: When is survey designed applied in Marketing?
flashcards.a: A survey designed before interviews usually asks the wrong questions; a survey designed after them can measure the right ones.

flashcards.q: When should before running not be used in Marketing?
flashcards.a: Before running the discount, the team should estimate whether it will lift volume by at least 50% among people who would not otherwise buy.

flashcards.q: Where does obtainable market come up in Marketing?
flashcards.a: Size a market from the bottom up and distinguish total, serviceable and obtainable market.

flashcards.q: Where does search not apply in Marketing?
flashcards.a: Search was where they confirmed a recommendation, not where they discovered it.

flashcards.q: Which approach to converts fits Marketing?
flashcards.a: Choice overload means that too many options can delay decisions, so a small number of clear packages often converts better than a long menu.

flashcards.q: Who is involved with hypothetical in Marketing?
flashcards.a: All companies, people and figures in the examples and case study are hypothetical and were built for teaching.

flashcards.q: Who should not be handling never in Marketing?
flashcards.a: A team that only researches and never acts produces reports instead of revenue.

flashcards.q: Why does unlike matter in Marketing?
flashcards.a: Unlike general-purpose scheduling tools, it was built around class waitlists and membership rules."

flashcards.q: How is paid acquisition used in Marketing?
flashcards.a: Work through a paid acquisition funnel from impressions to cost per customer.

flashcards.q: What does Marketing teach about statistically?
flashcards.a: Design an A/B test and judge whether a result is statistically meaningful.

flashcards.q: What should be avoided with agreement in Marketing?
flashcards.a: Without that agreement, marketing reports success on lead volume while sales complains about lead quality, and both are right.

flashcards.q: When is studios applied in Marketing?
flashcards.a: Interviews and a short survey suggest that 40% of studios already use some digital booking tool, which makes them easier to reach and quicker to switch, while the rest still rely on paper or messaging apps and rarely buy software in the first year.

flashcards.q: When should comparison pages not be used in Marketing?
flashcards.a: The right mix depends on the business: a product people actively search for may lean on search advertising and comparison pages; a new category with no search demand needs education and content first; a product whose buyers gather in communities may grow through community and partnerships.

flashcards.q: Where does positioning statement come up in Marketing?
flashcards.a: Segment a market, choose target segments with explicit criteria and write a positioning statement.

portion the company can realistically reach and serve with its current product, channels and geography
portion it can plausibly win over a defined period, given competition and its resources

overlap, expressed in the customer's words
set of associations people hold about a company or product: what it stands for, what it is like to deal with, whom it is for and what it promises
